title: Paper Tiger final trailer: James Gray explores a poisoned American dream
excerpt:
Neon releases the final trailer for James Gray's crime drama.
Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson star.
body_md:
Neon has released the final trailer for Paper Tiger, the latest crime drama from filmmaker James Gray. Starring Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson, the film is now playing nationwide in the United States after premiering in competition at Cannes and opening the New York Film Festival earlier in the fall. The new promotional material arrives as the distributor seeks to bring the film to a wider theatrical audience.

The central idea highlighted in the film's introduction is a troubling version of the American dream. In Gray's cinema, the pursuit of a better life rarely offers a straightforward path to happiness. Choices made with seemingly admirable intentions can have consequences that extend far beyond what the people making them originally imagined. That tension between aspiration and reality offers a useful framework for approaching his latest work without revealing its plot.

Gray has explored crime, family loyalty and moral compromise in earlier films such as The Yards and We Own the Night. His work in The Immigrant and Armageddon Time also examines the distance between America's promises and the lived experiences of individuals trying to find their place within society. His return to crime drama therefore represents an opportunity to revisit themes that have shaped much of his filmmaking career, rather than simply an exercise in genre conventions.

The cast is another notable attraction. Driver has demonstrated his ability to portray complicated characters in films including Marriage Story and Paterson. Teller is known for performances in Whiplash and Top Gun: Maverick, while Johansson has balanced major commercial productions with character-driven dramas such as Lost in Translation and Marriage Story. Bringing these performers together under Gray's direction creates considerable interest in how the film approaches its characters and their relationships.

The film's festival trajectory is also significant. A competition premiere at Cannes and an opening-night presentation at the New York Film Festival gave it visibility among audiences interested in auteur cinema before its wider release. Festival exposure does not necessarily translate into commercial success, however, and the nationwide theatrical rollout provides a different test of its appeal.

The final trailer was reported on November 24, 2026. The available feed entry does not specify the exact theatrical opening date or provide a detailed plot synopsis. For viewers interested in crime dramas that examine ambition, human relationships and the consequences of difficult choices, Paper Tiger offers a new opportunity to engage with the distinctive concerns of James Gray's cinema.
